programme: TEAD4, the Hippo-pathway effector that partners with YAP/TAZ, drives a proliferative/EMT programme through CCN2 (CTGF, the canonical Hippo-YAP output gene) and the angiogenic pair VEGFA/HIF1A/FGFR1, and is coupled in bladder-cancer literature to a TAZ/NRF2 antioxidant feedback loop. PER2, the core circadian repressor, directly transcribes the EMT-effector trio SNAI2/TWIST1/SERPINE1 that a Hippo-driven proliferative programme depends on. MAFF, a small-MAF partner of NRF2, sits at the same junction: it targets the paralogous clock gene PER1 and the NRF2 antioxidant-response gene GCLC. Read together this is a circadian-gated Hippo/EMT-redox axis, not three unrelated modules.
role_in_a: In bladder cancer this axis is directly documented: TEAD4/YAP-TAZ drives EMT via PI3K/AKT, sustains a TAZ/NRF2 proliferative feedback loop, and its target set (CCN2, VEGFA, HIF1A, FGFR1) is the angiogenic/CTGF output typical of Hippo-driven urothelial tumours; PER2 has separately been tied to circadian control of a heme-synthesis pathway in bladder cancer cells, consistent with clock input into the same proliferative programme.
role_in_b: In IBS the evidence is indirect. PER2 is documented in gut-epithelial and gut-circadian dysfunction (disturbed intestinal epithelial Per2 producing depression-like symptoms; clock-gene disruption in other gut-adjacent conditions), which is the flavor of epithelial/circadian disturbance proposed for IBS, but none of the retrieved papers name IBS itself. TEAD4 and MAFF have no recorded association or literature hit in IBS at all, so their role there is inferred from the shared programme, not observed.
shared_axis: If circadian control of Hippo-pathway output is a general feature of epithelial homeostasis, clock disruption acting through PER2/PER1 could unleash the same TEAD4-driven EMT/proliferative and MAFF/NRF2-linked oxidative-stress programme in both the urothelium and the colonic epithelium, producing proliferative signaling in one tissue and epithelial/motility disturbance in the other.
reasoning: TEAD4 is strongly and repeatedly documented in bladder cancer, and PER2 is documented in bladder cancer plus several circadian gut-epithelial contexts, so the module is nameable and partly evidenced. But nothing retrieved places this programme in IBS by name, MAFF carries no citation in either disease, and no source documents bladder cancer and IBS sharing this axis — the cross-disease claim rests on reasoning about circadian-epithelial biology, not on retrieved evidence.
support: PMID 41653270, 39934701, 40301305, 35581606 — place TEAD4/YAP-TAZ-TEAD in bladder cancer (EMT via PI3K/AKT, TAZ/NRF2 feedback loop, senescence signature, mitochondrial apoptosis). PMID 39682298 — places PER2 in bladder cancer via circadian control of a heme-synthesis pathway. PMID 40847793 — disturbed intestinal epithelial Per2 causing depression-like symptoms, a gut-epithelial circadian effect but not IBS by name. PMID 39896874, 39958687, 34211057 — clock-gene disruption in gut-adjacent conditions (post-infectious fatigue/long-COVID, hypothyroidism, thyroid-nodule sleep disruption), tangential to IBS but not IBS-specific. No publications were retrieved for MAFF in either disease.
how_to_falsify: Disrupt the core clock (PER2 knockdown or a PER2 loss-of-function mutant) in a bladder urothelial carcinoma line and separately in a colonic epithelial/enteric model, then measure TEAD4/YAP-TAZ output (CCN2, VEGFA) and the EMT trio (SNAI2, TWIST1, SERPINE1); if clock disruption fails to move Hippo output or EMT markers in either tissue, or TEAD4/MAFF activity proves independent of PER2/PER1 status, the proposed circadian-gated Hippo/EMT-redox link is wrong.
caveats: The 100 patient-group comparisons all derive from a single independent cohort pair (one bladder-cancer cohort, one IBS cohort, stratified many ways), not 100 independent replications. GATA6 and TBX2 were discordant and excluded even though GATA6's targets (WNT7B, MYOCD, TAGLN, MYH11) would fit a smooth-muscle/motility story — that alternative is not supported by the concordance data. DBP, a circadian output gene that would reinforce this narrative, appears only in the single-view exclusion list (0.17 recurrence) and must not be read as supporting evidence. MAFF's inclusion here rests on its target PER1, not on any retrieved literature about MAFF itself.
